back: A market with very many buyers and sellers of an identical product, perfect information and freedom of entry and exit, so each firm is a price-taker.

front: Revenue curves of a perfectly competitive firm?
back: P = AR = MR: a horizontal demand curve at the market price.
Produce where MC = MR = P, with MC rising.

front: What is the firm's short-run supply curve?
back: The part of its marginal cost curve above minimum average variable cost.
P = MR = MC = minimum ATC: normal profit and no entry or exit.

front: What happens when firms earn supernormal profit?
back: New firms enter, industry supply rises, price falls until only normal profit remains.

front: Productive and allocative efficiency in the long run?
back: Productively efficient (minimum ATC) and allocatively efficient (P = MC).
Any price below minimum average variable cost.

front: Weakness of perfect competition as a model?
back: Assumptions rarely hold; no supernormal profit for innovation, so dynamic efficiency may be low.
